title: Uniform level intervals imply the ordinary strict-tower domain
statement: Let ell be prime, E a finite extension of Q_ell, and base the recorded ordinary strict-tower presentation [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, def-sp-tower-shriek-realization]. Let T be a Noetherian scheme, with finite-level origins retaining specified cohomological and Tor intervals [def-sp-chart-tate-tower-data]. Let C be an actual ordinary derived strict coefficient tower on T whose levels are intrinsically constructible finite-Tor, with cohomological support in [a,b] and Tor amplitude in [s,t], where a<=b and s<=t. Then C has the recorded domain: its inverse realization is in the unnormalized uniform constructible finite-Tor subcategory for every abelian presentation, C is bounded below, and every level has an independent retained etale-origin witness. No transition compatibility is imposed on those witnesses.

proof.text: Exact evaluation in [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] commutes with kernels, images and quotients, hence $\mathcal H^i(K)_n=\mathcal H^i(K_n)$. For $i<a$ or $i>b$ all these evaluations are zero. A strict tower sheaf whose every component is zero is the zero object (all its transition maps are then uniquely zero), so $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ in those degrees. In particular $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Tow})$. This argument applies to every actual derived tower with common levelwise cohomological bounds; it uses no reconstruction of a tower from unrelated derived levels.

The section-preserving derived realization identifies the evaluated inverse realization with every original finite level. Transport its constructibility, cohomological and Tor intervals across these isomorphisms to obtain spConstructibleTorTowers for every abelian presentation. Apply the given finite-origins hypothesis to each original level, with its ordered intervals. The etale origin is bounded below, and the canonical intrinsic module equivalence identifies its fixed-scalar comparison with that original level. This supplies a separate retained Origin for each n, with no compatibility equation.
